bull_bear.body:
- Multi-feedstock flexibility - facilities 'equipped with multi-feedstock processing capabilities' able to run 'approximately 10-15 different feedstocks', which the AR ties explicitly to operational flexibility, supply-chain resilience and cost optimisation
- Scale after the Rajasthan expansion - biodiesel capacity at the Sirohi plant raised from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD, taking total installed annual capacity to approximately 4,80,000 KL of biodiesel and 63,000 KL of crude glycerine
- By-product integration - crude glycerine is refined on site into graded glycerin, converting a transesterification by-product into a saleable product line
- Carbon-credit certification as a differentiator - first Indian biodiesel company with Verra registration; world's first biodiesel project registered under the Voluntary Carbon Mechanism (VCS 3095); 57,874 credits accumulated for Sept 15, 2020 - March 31, 2022
- Zero-effluent discharge operations, cited alongside continuous R&D and technological innovation as underpinning the Company's position as 'one of India's leading manufacturers of green biofuels' (Corporate Governance Report - back-filled from the governance_entities bundle)
- Locational proximity to bulk buyers - 'Company supplies biodiesel to bulk buyers in its vicinity', and biodiesel traditionally trades cheaper than diesel in India, giving those buyers a cost saving
- Main Board migration - equity shares moved from the NSE Emerge Platform to the Main Board of both NSE and BSE during FY 2025-26, stated as reflecting continued growth and an enhanced corporate profile
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Feedstock availability and price volatility — 'Availability and prices of feedstocks such as used cooking oil and other renewable raw materials may fluctuate due to market dynamics, impacting production costs and margins.' This is the Company's first-listed risk and is structural: biodiesel economics are a spread between a volatile waste/vegetable-oil input and an OMC-set output price. The multi-feedstock platform (approximately 10-15 feedstocks) is the stated mitigant, giving substitution ability but not price protection.
- Customer concentration on Oil Marketing Companies — 'A significant portion of revenue comes from Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), potentially exposing the Company to risks associated with reliance on a limited customer base.' The AR names no other channel of comparable size beyond local bulk buyers, so a small set of state-linked buyers effectively sets both volume and price.
- Dependence on OMC procurement programmes and tender/indent timing — 'Procurement programmes and tender schedules of Oil Marketing Companies play an important role in the biodiesel market. Changes in procurement volumes or timelines may affect sales performance.' This risk materialised in FY26: management states that 'delays in the issuance of Purchase Orders (POs) and Indents despite sizable tender allocations led to elevated inventory levels and impacted short-term margins' - i.e. an allocation win does not convert to revenue on the Company's own timetable, and the shortfall lands in working capital.
- Regulatory and policy dependence — 'The biofuel industry is influenced by Government policies relating to procurement, blending programmes, taxation and environmental regulations. Any significant changes in these policies may impact business operations.' The entire demand thesis rests on the National Policy on Biofuels and the blending trajectory - the AR itself notes blending is currently below 1% against a Government goal of 5% by 2030 - so policy slippage removes the growth driver rather than merely delaying it.
- Commodity and energy price risk - biodiesel's competitiveness versus diesel — 'Fluctuations in crude oil prices and energy costs may influence the competitiveness of biodiesel compared to conventional fuels and affect overall industry dynamics.' Bulk-buyer demand is explicitly a price-arbitrage proposition - 'Traditionally, biodiesel trades cheaper than diesel in India, offering bulk buyers an opportunity to cut costs' - so a fall in crude erodes the discretionary, non-OMC part of the book.
- Operational and supply-chain risk at the manufacturing sites — 'Manufacturing operations are exposed to risks associated with plant operations, equipment reliability, utilities, logistics and supply chain disruptions.' With only two plants - Sirohi (Rajasthan) and Anand (Gujarat) - and the enlarged capacity concentrated at Sirohi, an outage at a single site is a company-level event. The stated mitigation is strengthened operational processes and preventive maintenance systems.
- Utilisation risk on the enlarged capacity base — Structural rather than labelled: the Company has taken Rajasthan biodiesel capacity from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD and total installed annual capacity to approximately 4,80,000 KL, while naming 'increasing capacity utilisation' as a continuing focus and disclosing no utilisation percentage or production volume anywhere in the routed text. Fixed-cost absorption therefore depends on OMC offtake the Company does not control.
- Single-product concentration on biodiesel — Structural rather than labelled: 'Biodiesel forms the core of Kotyark's product portfolio.' The routed text describes no segment other than biodiesel and its by-products (Veg Ester semi-finished and crude/refined glycerine), and the glycerin refining step is still at pilot scale (a 210 KL/day pilot plant at Sirohi), so the diversification is real but early.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures biodiesel - a renewable, biodegradable fuel produced by transesterification of vegetable oils, waste oils, animal fats, tallow and used cooking oil - at two plants, at Sirohi (Rajasthan) and Anand (Gujarat), and sells it to Oil Marketing Companies for blending into diesel and speed-diesel and to bulk buyers such as transport contractors, mining companies and industries in the plants' vicinity. Alongside biodiesel it sells Veg Ester (semi-finished biodiesel, sold on to other processing units) and crude glycerine, the by-product of transesterification, which it has begun refining on site into graded glycerin for food, pharmaceutical, cosmetic and carpet-manufacturing uses. Incorporated in December 2016 as a biofuel trader, it built its first plant in 2019, listed on NSE Emerge in November 2021 and migrated to the NSE and BSE Main Boards during FY 2025-26.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Bio-Diesel:** Biodiesel (B100 / neat biodiesel; mono alkyl ester) produced by transesterification of vegetable oil, animal fats, tallow and used cooking oil, Biodiesel supplied to OMCs for blending in diesel and premium-category speed-diesel, Biodiesel supplied to bulk buyers - transport contractors, mining companies and industries in the vicinity of the plants
- **Veg Ester-Semi Finished:** Veg Ester - semi-finished biodiesel that, with further processing, is converted into biodiesel; sold to other processing units for generation of biodiesel
- **Crude Glycerin:** Crude glycerin - by-product of the transesterification reaction; 'the production of 100 litres of biodiesel yields about 14 litres of crude glycerin', Refined glycerin in different grades, produced by further refining crude glycerin in an on-site processing plant, for food, pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications
- **Carbon credits:** Carbon credits registered and issued under Verra; 57,874 carbon credits accumulated for the period September 15, 2020 to March 31, 2022

outlook.body:
- Increase capacity utilisation of the enlarged biodiesel asset base rather than add new capacity - 'The Company continues to focus on improving operational efficiency, increasing capacity utilisation, strengthening its raw material sourcing network and expanding its participation in tenders issued by Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).' (Corporate Overview - back-filled from the profile / capex_expansion bundles; this bundle's own sections carry no strategy text)
- Win a larger share of OMC procurement - expanding participation in OMC tenders is named as the primary route to market, and management notes OMCs are now moving to direct Letters of Intent, which has 'significantly improved' execution visibility (Outlook - back-filled from the risks_esg bundle)
- Strengthen and diversify raw-material sourcing, using the plants' ability to run approximately 10-15 different feedstocks for supply-chain resilience and cost optimisation
- Move down the glycerine chain - refine crude glycerine on site into graded glycerin for food, pharmaceutical and cosmetic uses, adding a second product line to the biodiesel core (back-filled from the profile / risks_esg bundles)
- Build 'a sustainable, integrated and scalable green energy platform' by expanding market presence, improving manufacturing efficiencies and adopting advanced technologies
- Pursue carbon-reduction and carbon-credit monetisation as a distinct opportunity - 'Growing focus on carbon reduction and environmental sustainability presents opportunities through green initiatives and potential participation in carbon credit and sustainability-linked programmes.'
- Sustain investment in machinery, skilled workforce and manufacturing capability - 'Our commitment to quality, innovation, and operational efficiency remains at the core of our strategy. This is reflected in our sustained investments in state-of-the-art machinery, a highly skilled workforce, and comprehensive manufacturing capabilities.'
- The Company retains rather than reserves: 'Your directors have not apportioned any amount to the General Reserves. Full amount of net profit is carried to Reserve & Surplus account.' For FY 2025-26 the Board, at its meeting on April 27, 2026, recommended a Final Dividend of Rs 5.00 per equity share of Rs 10.00 face value, subject to shareholder approval at the 10th AGM convened for August 22, 2026 by video conferencing; it is to be paid out of the profits of the financial year, within the time prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 and subject to TDS. Separately, the members approved a Bonus Issue by Postal Ballot on June 15, 2026 in the ratio of 10:1 (ten bonus equity shares for every one existing equity share held) on the 1,02,79,116 equity shares of Rs 10 each; the AGM resolution provides that if the bonus shares are allotted before the dividend is paid, the AGGREGATE dividend payout stays unchanged and the per-share dividend is proportionately adjusted downward on the expanded paid-up capital - i.e. the policy commitment is to a fixed total rupee payout, not to a fixed dividend per share. The Board (or a committee) is authorised to determine the revised per-share dividend. No formal Dividend Distribution Policy text, no payout-ratio target, no buyback, no debt-reduction target and no credit rating appear in any routed section.
- Carbon-credit certification under Verra - approval received for registration and issuance of carbon credits, stated to make Kotyark 'the first Indian Company in the Bio-Diesel sector to obtain this prestigious recognition'; 57,874 carbon credits accumulated for the period September 15, 2020 to March 31, 2022.
- Registration under the Voluntary Carbon Mechanism (VCS, GS, GCC etc.) with Project ID: VCS 3095, recognised by Infinite Solutions as 'the world's first project to produce biodiesel registered under the Voluntary Carbon Mechanism'; Certificate of Recognition received from Infinite Solutions, described as the first company from India to join the UNFCCC Carbon Neutral Initiative.
- Zero-effluent discharge operations - 'With its zero-effluent discharge operations, continuous focus on research and development, technological innovation, and operational excellence, Kotyark Industries Limited continues to strengthen its position as one of India's leading manufacturers of green biofuels.' (Corporate Governance Report - back-filled from the governance_entities bundle; the risks_esg bundle does not carry it.)
- Waste-based, circular feedstock as the core input - used cooking oil, waste oils, animal fats, tallow and recycled restaurant grease are converted into fuel, described as 'utilising waste materials and renewable resources to create a viable alternative to conventional diesel'.
- Product-level emissions benefit as the business rationale - biodiesel 'has virtually no sulfur, owing to which reduces the emission of hydrocarbons, NOx, carbon monoxide, and ozone formation' and 'minimizes the particulate discharge from engines at any concentration'; the Company positions itself as supporting India's clean energy transition and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
- Stated intent to participate further in carbon markets - 'Growing focus on carbon reduction and environmental sustainability presents opportunities through green initiatives and potential participation in carbon credit and sustainability-linked programmes.' Framed as an opportunity, with no tonnage, revenue or date attached.
- By-product valorisation rather than disposal - crude glycerine from transesterification is refined on site into graded glycerin for food, pharmaceutical and cosmetic uses instead of being sold off or discarded.
- NO QUANTIFIED ESG TARGET IS DISCLOSED anywhere in the routed text - no emissions intensity, energy, water, waste or safety metric, no net-zero or reduction target with a date, and no diversity or workforce data. See notes: no BRSR was routed for this company and the CSR annexure was not routed either, so this is a delivery gap on top of a genuinely target-free narrative.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Kotyark runs two manufacturing facilities - Sirohi (Rajasthan), its first plant, built in 2019, and Anand (Gujarat). The one named expansion project in the routed text is the Rajasthan debottlenecking/expansion: 'Last year the Company expanded the biodiesel production capacity at its Rajasthan facility from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD, significantly strengthening its manufacturing capabilities. Consequently, the Company's total installed annual production capacity increased to approximately 4,80,000 KL of biodiesel and 63,000 KL of crude glycerine.' The AR gives no commissioning date, no cost and no as-of date for this project, and 'Last year' is undated - in an FY 2025-26 report it may mean FY 2024-25 or may be a paragraph carried over from the prior year's AR; nothing was inferred. The second project is a downstream one: the Company 'took a significant step forward by installing a glycerin processing pilot plant with a capacity of 210 KL per day at its Sirohi facility', supporting its move from selling crude glycerine to refining it on site into graded glycerin (this sentence reaches only the risks_esg bundle - the copy of the same Corporate Overview spread routed to capex_expansion is truncated before it). Anand has no separately stated capacity. Beyond these, management describes no new plant, line, brownfield or greenfield project and no capex programme: forward intent is expressed only as utilising the enlarged base - 'improving operational efficiency, increasing capacity utilisation, strengthening its raw material sourcing network and expanding its participation in tenders issued by Oil Marketing Companies' - plus generic intent to expand market presence, improve manufacturing efficiencies and adopt advanced technologies while 'building a sustainable, integrated and scalable green energy platform'. The Company also completed a listing-status change during FY 2025-26, migrating its shares from the NSE Emerge Platform to the Main Board of both NSE and BSE.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Policy-driven blending demand: 'At present blending in biodiesel less than 1%, with Indian Government setting a goal to take this level to 5% by 2030' - the gap between current and target blending is the stated volume driver
- OMC procurement mechanics are the swing factor: FY26 saw 'delays in the issuance of Purchase Orders (POs) and Indents despite sizable tender allocations', which 'led to elevated inventory levels and impacted short-term margins'; the shift to direct LOIs is presented as the fix (back-filled from the risks_esg bundle's Outlook)
- More tenders expected: 'Additionally, more tenders are expected to open shortly' - the sentence is cut off in the routed text, so what it promised is not readable
- Government policy support - the National Policy on Biofuels and OMC procurement initiatives are named as the structural underpinning of Indian biodiesel demand
- Energy-security substitution - India's effort to reduce dependence on imported crude oil and raise use of domestically produced renewable fuels is expected to create long-term growth opportunities for the biofuel sector
- India's Net Zero by 2070 commitment and the Economic Survey 2025-26's emphasis on renewable energy, green hydrogen and biofuels as energy-security levers
- Enlarged capacity as a demand-capture lever - 'The enhanced production capacity positions the Company to meet the growing demand for biodiesel arising from increasing blending initiatives and industrial consumption'
- Multi-feedstock processing and continuous production-technology improvement are expected to enhance operational efficiency, optimise costs and improve competitiveness
- Global market backdrop: global biodiesel market valued at USD 40.26 billion in 2025, projected to grow from USD 42.67 billion in 2026 to USD 67.4 billion by 2034 at a 6.75% CAGR, with Europe holding 41.92% share in 2025
- Global macro backdrop cited: IMF global GDP growth projected at 3.0% in 2025 and 3.1% in 2026, with trade uncertainty, geopolitical risk and fiscal pressure flagged as challenges
- Margin/competitiveness swing from crude: 'Fluctuations in crude oil prices and energy costs may influence the competitiveness of biodiesel compared to conventional fuels'; biodiesel traditionally trades cheaper than diesel in India, which is what attracts bulk buyers
- Feedstock cost is the principal margin driver - availability and prices of used cooking oil and other renewable raw materials 'may fluctuate due to market dynamics, impacting production costs and margins'
- 'Encouragingly, Kotyark received LOIs worth Rs 223.53 crores during FY 2025-26period, laying a good start for FY26 performance.' - Letters of Intent from Oil Marketing Companies received during FY 2025-26. (Back-filled from the risks_esg bundle's Outlook paragraph; the sentence is printed with a run-together 'FY 2025-26period' and the concluding year reads FY26 where the surrounding text is about FY27 - see notes.)
- 'Additionally, more tenders are expected to open shortly, which' - the pipeline statement is truncated mid-sentence in the routed text; no tender count, value or date is readable
- No order book, backlog or unexecuted-order value as at March 31, 2026 is disclosed in any routed section - the LOI figure above is an inflow-during-the-year number, not a closing backlog
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Kotyark Industries is a Gujarat/Rajasthan-based manufacturer of biodiesel and glycerine from multi-source renewable and waste feedstocks, selling principally into Oil Marketing Company tenders and local bulk buyers, and is the first Indian biodiesel company to obtain Verra carbon-credit registration.

open.item: Management flags that OMC delays in issuing Purchase Orders and Indents against sizable tender allocations left the Company with elevated inventory and compressed short-term margins in FY26, and is relying on the OMCs' move to direct LOIs to fix execution visibility.

The Company will continue improving operational efficiency, increasing capacity utilisation, strengthening its raw-material sourcing network and expanding its participation in tenders issued by Oil Marketing Companies.

The Company intends to strengthen its position in renewable energy by expanding market presence, improving manufacturing efficiencies and adopting advanced technologies, building 'a sustainable, integrated and scalable green energy platform'.
The Company will keep expanding its participation in OMC tenders while improving operational efficiency and capacity utilisation and strengthening raw-material sourcing.
The Company's stated forward lever is raising utilisation of the enlarged capacity rather than adding new capacity; no utilisation percentage, production volume or target is disclosed.

risks.note: 'Procurement programmes and tender schedules of Oil Marketing Companies play an important role in the biodiesel market. Changes in procurement volumes or timelines may affect sales performance.' This risk materialised in FY26: management states that 'delays in the issuance of Purchase Orders (POs) and Indents despite sizable tender allocations led to elevated inventory levels and impacted short-term margins' - i.e. an allocation win does not convert to revenue on the Company's own timetable, and the shortfall lands in working capital.
risks.risk: Dependence on OMC procurement programmes and tender/indent timing

risks.note: 'The biofuel industry is influenced by Government policies relating to procurement, blending programmes, taxation and environmental regulations. Any significant changes in these policies may impact business operations.' The entire demand thesis rests on the National Policy on Biofuels and the blending trajectory - the AR itself notes blending is currently below 1% against a Government goal of 5% by 2030 - so policy slippage removes the growth driver rather than merely delaying it.

'Fluctuations in crude oil prices and energy costs may influence the competitiveness of biodiesel compared to conventional fuels and affect overall industry dynamics.' Bulk-buyer demand is explicitly a price-arbitrage proposition - 'Traditionally, biodiesel trades cheaper than diesel in India, offering bulk buyers an opportunity to cut costs' - so a fall in crude erodes the discretionary, non-OMC part of the book.
risks.risk: Commodity and energy price risk - biodiesel's competitiveness versus diesel

risks.note: 'Manufacturing operations are exposed to risks associated with plant operations, equipment reliability, utilities, logistics and supply chain disruptions.' With only two plants - Sirohi (Rajasthan) and Anand (Gujarat) - and the enlarged capacity concentrated at Sirohi, an outage at a single site is a company-level event. The stated mitigation is strengthened operational processes and preventive maintenance systems.
risks.risk: Operational and supply-chain risk at the manufacturing sites

risks.note: Structural rather than labelled: the Company has taken Rajasthan biodiesel capacity from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD and total installed annual capacity to approximately 4,80,000 KL, while naming 'increasing capacity utilisation' as a continuing focus and disclosing no utilisation percentage or production volume anywhere in the routed text. Fixed-cost absorption therefore depends on OMC offtake the Company does not control.
risks.risk: Utilisation risk on the enlarged capacity base

risks.note: Structural rather than labelled: 'Biodiesel forms the core of Kotyark's product portfolio.' The routed text describes no segment other than biodiesel and its by-products (Veg Ester semi-finished and crude/refined glycerine), and the glycerin refining step is still at pilot scale (a 210 KL/day pilot plant at Sirohi), so the diversification is real but early.

meta.thesis: Kotyark Industries is a Gujarat/Rajasthan-based manufacturer of biodiesel and glycerine from multi-source renewable and waste feedstocks, selling principally into Oil Marketing Company tenders and local bulk buyers, and is the first Indian biodiesel company to obtain Verra carbon-credit registration.
